intro: The third condition: a past that can no longer be changed. And how the three kinds of «si» fit together.
p.hubiera.consejo: It is the imperfect subjunctive of «haber». With a participle it forms «si hubiera sabido». The h is silent.
p.hubieras.consejo: It is the tú form: «si hubieras mirado el móvil, lo habrías visto».
p.habría ido.consejo: It is the conditional perfect: it goes in the result of «si + hubiera»: «si lo hubiera sabido, habría ido».
p.si lo hubiera sabido.consejo: It is the complete unreal past condition. The «lo» is the fact that was not known.
p.de haberlo sabido.consejo: «De» plus the compound infinitive replaces a condition with «si». It sounds a little more formal.
p.contestar.consejo: It is regular in -ar: «contestó», «te habría contestado». It is used with calls, messages and questions.
p.oportunidad.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -dad: «una oportunidad». The stress falls on the end: o-por-tu-ni-DAD.
p.a tiempo.consejo: It means «not arriving late»: «llegó a tiempo». It never changes.
p.genial.consejo: It is informal and works for masculine and feminine: «un plan genial», «una fiesta genial».
p.batería.consejo: It is feminine: «la batería». The accent on «í» separates the vowels: ba-te-RÍ-a.
b1.titulo: A past that no longer changes
b1.texto:
To imagine a different past you need two forms with **haber**:

- **Si** + **hubiera** + participle → the condition that did not happen.
- **Habría** + participle → the result that did not happen.

Example: **Si lo hubiera sabido, habría ido.** (I did not know, and I did not go.)

It is the «impossible» past: it can no longer be changed, only imagined.
b2.f1.texto: If I had known, I would have gone.
b2.f2.texto: If you had looked at your phone, you would have seen it.
b2.f3.texto: Had I seen it, I would have answered you.
b2.f4.texto: If you had come, you would now know my brother.
b2.f5.texto: Then I have lost a good opportunity.
b2.f6.texto: You can still get there in time for the next one.
b2.f7.texto: Next time I will charge the battery earlier.
b4.texto:
The whole system fits into three patterns:

- **Possible**: si + present → present, future or command. **Si tengo** tiempo, **iré**.
- **Unreal now**: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional. **Si tuviera** tiempo, **iría**.
- **Unreal in the past**: si + pluperfect subjunctive → conditional perfect. **Si hubiera tenido** tiempo, **habría ido**.

Sometimes the condition and the result speak of different times: **Si hubiera aceptado** el trabajo, **ahora viviría** en Chile.

The forms in **-ra** and in **-se** are equal: si hubiera sabido / si hubiese sabido. Never put the conditional after **si**: «si habría sabido» is a mistake.

You can also say **de** + compound infinitive: **De haberlo sabido**, habría ido.
b4.e0.texto: If I had studied more, I would have passed.
b4.e1.texto: If I had accepted the job, I would now live in Chile.
b4.e2.texto: Had we arrived earlier, we would have had dinner together.
b5.f0.texto: One rainy afternoon, Pablo opens a drawer and finds a crumpled invitation.
b5.f1.texto: The paper smells of dust and old perfume.
b5.f2.texto: A golden ink announces the date of the party in the corner.
b5.f3.texto: Three weeks have passed since that night.
b5.f4.texto: Pablo strokes the edge of the paper with a sad finger.
b5.f5.texto: If he had opened that drawer earlier, he would have seen the invitation in time.
b5.f6.texto: He would have danced until late under the coloured lights.
b5.f7.texto: Now he only hears the soft tap of the rain against the window.
b5.f8.texto: Even so, he does not regret that absence too much.
b5.f9.texto: He leaves the invitation on the desk, next to the lit lamp.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That speaks of now, not of the party that already took place.
b6.o1: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría ido.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «Hubiera sabido» and «habría ido» look at the past.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is colloquial and does not mark an unreal condition.
b6.pregunta: You did not go to the party. Which sentence regrets it correctly?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «si + hubiera + participle» is the unreal condition of the past.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Había sabido» is a real fact; it does not work after an unreal «si».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Habría» is the result; it never goes after «si».
b7.pregunta: It is the condition of an unreal past.
b8.frase: Si hubieras venido, ahora conocerías a mi hermano
b8.traduccion: If you had come, you would now know my brother
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! «De + compound infinitive» replaces «si + hubiera».
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Si lo viera» speaks of the present, not the past.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Si lo veo» is a real, possible condition.
b10.frase: Si hubieras mirado el móvil, lo ____ visto.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Has visto» is present perfect; it does not express an imagined result.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Habías visto» is a real past, not an imagined one.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Correct: the imagined result takes the conditional perfect.
b10.pregunta: It is the result of an unreal past.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «If I had known, I would have gone.»
b12.o0: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría un título.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes! The condition is past and the result is from now.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Both verbs speak of the past: there is no mixing.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is a real present condition, with no imagined past.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence mixes an imagined past and a present?
p.mirado.consejo: Participle of «mirar». With «hubieras» it forms «si hubieras mirado». The stress is on «RA».
p.haberlo.consejo: The infinitive «haber» with «lo» attached. In «haberlo visto», «lo» goes with «visto».
p.contestado.consejo: Participle of «contestar». With «habría» it forms «te habría contestado». The stress is on «TA».
p.conocerías.consejo: Conditional of «conocer» for tú. The c sounds like th, and the accent on «í» separates the vowels.
p.llegas.consejo: Present of «llegar» for tú. The g becomes gu before e: «llegues»; before a it stays g.
p.cargaré.consejo: Future of «cargar» for yo. The accent on the final «é» marks the stress: kar-ga-RÉ.
p.estudiado.consejo: Participle of «estudiar». With «hubiera» it forms «si hubiera estudiado». The «ia» sounds as one beat.
p.aprobado.consejo: Participle of «aprobar». With «habría» it forms «habría aprobado». It is the opposite of «suspender».
p.aceptado.consejo: Participle of «aceptar». The c before t sounds th: a-thep-TA-do. With «hubiera»: «hubiera aceptado».
p.viviría.consejo: Conditional of «vivir»: infinitive plus «-ía». The v sounds like b: bi-bi-RÍ-a.
p.habríamos.consejo: Conditional of «haber» for nosotros. With a participle: «habríamos cenado». The accent separates i-a.
p.cenado.consejo: The past participle of «cenar». It comes after «haber» here.
p.invitación.consejo: It ends in «-ción», like «nación»; the c before i sounds like th in Spain.
p.arrugada.consejo: It comes from «arrugar» and ends in «-ada» to agree with a feminine noun.
p.polvo.consejo: The v sounds like b in Spanish, so say POL-bo.
p.tinta.consejo: «Tinta» is the ink for writing; «tinte» is a dye, so do not mix them up.
p.anuncia.consejo: From «anunciar». The c before i sounds like th in Spain.
p.pasado.consejo: The participle of «pasar». With «han» it means «have passed».
p.semanas.consejo: Plural of «semana». The final -s is a soft hiss.
p.acaricia.consejo: From «acariciar», to stroke gently. The «-cia» ending reads «thya».
p.borde.consejo: The r between vowels is a single soft tap: BOR-de.
p.dedo.consejo: A short word with the stress on the first syllable: DE-do.
p.bailado.consejo: The participle of «bailar». The «-ado» ending is for -ar verbs.
p.contra.consejo: Opposite of «a favor de»; it means against or touching, as in «contra la ventana».
p.arrepiente.consejo: From «arrepentirse». The «ie» forms one sound: pien.
p.ausencia.consejo: The «-cia» ending reads «thya», and the stress falls on SEN.
p.escritorio.consejo: The end «-io» is one quick sound, like «ryo».
p.encendida.consejo: Feminine of «encendido»; it agrees with «lámpara», so it ends in -a.
p.sabido.consejo: The participle of «saber», used with «haber» as in «habría sabido».
p.título.consejo: It has an accent because the stress falls on the first syllable: TI-tu-lo.
